# the contributor audit of the exact cubic ear first variation

Source: `candidate 3d7872ba08080216`, Sections 1--6. Verdict: PASS for the stated local result. This audit reads the actual source proof; Slab's separate audit also passes.

For a fixed piecewise affine continuous edge roof, the area Jacobian is one and the cap-area variation is its integral over each unchanged signature interval. The crossing shifts contribute only second order to area. A transverse section crossing contributes a multiple of the roof value at that crossing; these are exactly the two atoms, not missing area terms. At a tight triangle the already proved all-triangle cubic makes every vertex derivative zero. The two adjacent outward normal components of a vertex motion are independent. Thus the two edge moments vanish separately, as required by the Green argument.

The Green kernel has second derivative minus a point mass. Its endpoint slopes are the two vanishing moments. This gives the two negative outer quadratics and the middle quadratic with coefficient beta_s. Minimizing A/z+B/(1-z) gives the stated square-root criterion, with endpoints already strictly negative. The positivity of each alpha follows from the archived completed-square inequality; it is not inferred from a raw double-area derivative.

The disk proof is complete. Its gap is concave in r because the only nonlinear term is a positive multiple of the geometric mean of two positive affine functions. At the upper endpoint the negative squared-discriminant identity proves a positive gap irrespective of the sign of Z. At zero the signed roots obey U z_1+V z_2=U+V-1. When both are nonnegative their sum is less than one. Otherwise the affine difference R-Lt is positive at both ends of the full feasible interval, and b^2<=1 supplies the comparison of squares. These cover every endpoint possibility; concavity transfers strictness throughout.

The substitution retains the actual equality geometry: p,q in (0,1), D>0, F+G=1, a=1-V, b=U, U+V>1, and 0<r<FG. The scale in the raw derivative is C/(2k), and beta_s=alpha_i+alpha_j-C/(2k) counts total area once. Thus the disk inequality is precisely the coupled geometric ear criterion, including the two section atoms.

The conclusion is strict first variation for each fixed interior peak of an outward triangular ear at a strict-incidence tight triangle. No finite-ear monotonicity, uniform remainder at vertex peaks, arbitrary quadrilateral theorem, or mixed-integer result is implied. Weak-incidence limits would also require a separate argument and are not silently included.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
